gloss: to hold out; to present; to submit

definitions.explanation: To stretch out one's hand or an object toward someone.
To formally offer or present something to someone.
To submit documents or send mail.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{笑顔|えがお}で{手|て}を{差|さ}し{出|だ}した。
examples.english: She held out her hand with a smile.

examples.japanese: {名刺|めいし}を{差|さ}し{出|だ}して{自己紹介|じこしょうかい}した。
examples.english: I presented my business card and introduced myself.

examples.japanese: {差出人|さしだしにん}の{住所|じゅうしょ}が{書|か}いてなかった。

notes:
{差|さ}し{出|だ}す is a transitive verb ({他動詞|たどうし}) formed from {差|さ}す (to hold up) + {出|だ}す (to put out). It suggests a polite or formal gesture of offering.

ASPECT (ている):
{差|さ}し{出|だ}している indicates the ongoing action of holding something out.

PARTICLE PATTERNS:
- [thing]を{差|さ}し{出|だ}す — to hold out/present [thing]
- [person]に[thing]を{差|さ}し{出|だ}す — to present [thing] to [person]

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {手|て}を{差|さ}し{出|だ}す (hold out one's hand)
- {名刺|めいし}を{差|さ}し{出|だ}す (present a business card)
- {手紙|てがみ}を{差|さ}し{出|だ}す (send a letter)

RELATED WORDS:
- {差出人|さしだしにん}: sender (of mail)
- {差|さ}し{入|い}れ: gift brought when visiting

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {出|だ}す: to take out (neutral)
- {提出|ていしゅつ}する: to submit (formal documents)
